title: Officer had no choice but to shoot Bennis: Coroner
article: A Quebec coroner says a police officer had no choice but to shoot Mohamed Anas Bennis, a Montreal man who died in 2005.
The coroner's office released its report on the 25-year-old's death Thursday.
Bennis was shot to death by police on Dec. 1, 2005 after leaving a mosque in the city's Côte-des-Neiges district.
During the coroner's inquest police testified that Bennis attacked an officer with a knife before he was shot.
In her report, coroner Catherine Rudel-Tessier said the police officers involved acted in self-defense, and had no other option to protect themselves.
The coroner said the reason Bennis attacked the officer is still unknown.
The inquest into Bennis' death took place in April, after Montreal's police union attempted to block it.
